title: Descent of a termwise coefficient map through a resolving counit
statement: Let A and B be abelian categories with chosen unbounded derived categories in independent Hom universes. Let E:A -> B and V:B -> A be additive functors, with V exact, and let i:id_A -> E followed by V be a natural transformation. Let (F,epsilon) be a universal left derived pair for termwise E followed by derived localization. Equip F with a coherent integer shift for which epsilon commutes with shifts. Let P be any property of A-complexes such that every complex admits a quasi-isomorphism from a member of P and epsilon is invertible at all members of P. There exists a natural transformation eta:id_D(A) -> F followed by derived V. At every complex K, eta_(QK), followed by derived V of epsilon_K and the exact derived restriction comparison, equals Q applied to the termwise map i_K. Moreover eta commutes with the degree-one composite canonical shift. This statement includes no assertion that F preserves distinguished triangles.

source.place: derived.tex, Tag 06XN (lemma-find-existence-computes), Tag 05SU (lemma-derived-shift), and lemma-compose-derived-functors-general, whose proof explicitly pulls an essentially constant limit through a functor; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 06YY supplies the parent coefficient application.

proof.text: On homotopy categories resolve the vertices of right fractions by P. The resolving-class essential-constancy argument gives denominator limits computed by a P-resolution. Every functor preserves these essentially constant limits, so the counit postcomposed with derived V is still a right Kan extension. Lift the localized termwise coefficient map into this universal pair. Its defining factorization gives the displayed comparison on every complex.

Postcomposition with a shift equivalence preserves right Kan extensions. The two shifted lifts satisfy the same counit equation because the termwise map, epsilon and the restriction comparison commute with shifts. Uniqueness of the shifted universal lift identifies them.

theorem exists_derivedCoefficientMap
    {A : Type u} [Category.{v} A] [Abelian A]
    {B : Type u'} [Category.{v'} B] [Abelian B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} A] [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} B]
    (E : A ⥤ B) [E.Additive] (V : B ⥤ A) [V.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits V] [PreservesFiniteColimits V]
    (ι : 𝟭 A ⟶ E ⋙ V)
    (F : DerivedCategory A ⥤ DerivedCategory B)
    (ε : DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ F ⟶ E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q)
    [F.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomologicalComplex.quasiIso A (.up ℤ))]
    [F.CommShift ℤ] [NatTrans.CommShift ε ℤ]
    (P : ObjectProperty (CochainComplex A ℤ))
    (hres : ∀ K, ∃ (L : CochainComplex A ℤ) (p : L ⟶ K), P L ∧ QuasiIso p)
    (hε : ∀ K, P K → IsIso (ε.app K)) :
    ∃ η : 𝟭 (DerivedCategory A) ⟶ F ⋙ V.mapDerivedCategory,
      (∀ K : CochainComplex A ℤ,
        η.app (DerivedCategory.Q.obj K) ≫ V.mapDerivedCategory.map (ε.app K) ≫
          V.mapDerivedCategoryFactors.hom.app ((E.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj K) =
        DerivedCategory.Q.map
          ((Functor.mapHomologicalComplexIdIso A (.up ℤ)).inv.app K ≫
            (NatTrans.mapHomologicalComplex ι (.up ℤ)).app K ≫
            (Functor.mapHomologicalComplexCompIso (Iso.refl (E ⋙ V)) (.up ℤ)).inv.app K)) ∧
      (∀ X : DerivedCategory A,
        η.app ((shiftFunctor _ (1 : ℤ)).obj X) ≫
          ((F ⋙ V.mapDerivedCategory).commShiftIso (1 : ℤ)).hom.app X =
        (shiftFunctor _ (1 : ℤ)).map (η.app X))
